## Where to experience wildlife in Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay are among its principal countries, but **they are not the only ones**. The route passes through Bolivia and Peru between the Chilean and Ecuadorian stages.

The “Wildlife and Safaris” theme applies to the tour as a whole and does not promise a separate safari in all four countries. Deserts, rocks and reservoirs fall under the separate Nature theme. According to the confirmed itinerary, the most substantial wildlife watching takes place in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Chile offers contrasting desert scenery, Colombia rocky landscapes and reservoirs near Guatapé, while Uruguay is represented by a day visit to its capital.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Ecuador: giant tortoises and island ecosystems

After [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), travelers fly to Baltra and cross to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The itinerary includes a [Santa Cruz highlands excursion](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/), featuring giant tortoises and lava tunnels. The contrast between the island's natural zones is visible during the transfer from the drier north toward the green highlands and Puerto Ayora.

The following day includes **one marine excursion chosen from two alternatives**, not both:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach. The description of this option mentions colonies of frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies, sea lions and marine iguanas.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión. This is a different island route; the specific arrangements and choice of option are confirmed at booking.

For travelers who come to see a particular bird species or island, this choice is crucial. A North Seymour visit cannot be assumed if the second option is confirmed. Even on the chosen island, sightings of specific animals depend on nature, the season and excursion conditions.

The Galápagos include protected land and marine areas with special visiting regulations. Agreeing an authorized route, guiding arrangements, environmental rules and boarding times matters more than any promise to “see all the animals.” Compare other [Ecuador tours under Wildlife and Safaris](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Chile: Atacama landscapes, but no advertised safari

From [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), travelers fly to Calama and travel to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The dry climate, desert valleys and high-altitude Andes are the main natural attractions. However, the Chilean stage of this 32-day tour primarily involves capital-city sightseeing and preparation for the journey into Bolivia, not a separate wildlife-watching program.

The route then continues on jeep excursions through Bolivian lagoons and salt flats. These are important scenic highlights of the complete journey, but they belong to **Bolivia**, not Chile. Wildlife or stops in a neighboring country must not be attributed to Chile merely because they lie along the same high-altitude route.

If Chilean nature is your main interest, compare [nature tours including Chile](/interests/nature/tours/chile/) by the reserves, walks and time outside cities actually included.

## Colombia: Guatapé's rocks and water, without promises of wildlife sightings

In the Colombian section, an excursion from [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) visits [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The natural attractions are the granite monolith, hilly scenery and reservoir. The same day includes a walk through the town's colorful streets.

The journey then continues through [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). Historic and sightseeing excursions are included in both cities. These should not be replaced with promises of birdwatching, an Amazon rainforest excursion or rare-animal encounters: no such stand-alone activities appear in the selected itinerary.

For a nature-oriented trip, compare [routes including nature in Colombia](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/), where the amount of time spent outdoors may differ.

## Uruguay: a cultural stop without a nature excursion

Travelers reach [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) by ferry from Buenos Aires for a day visit, then return. The tour includes city sightseeing with an English-speaking guide and some free time. No natural park visit, birdwatching or time in a national reserve is specified for this day in Uruguay.

Uruguay therefore broadens the trip's geography in this selection but **does not add a separate wildlife stage**. Travelers interested in Uruguay's nature would need a separately arranged program. When comparing [nature tours including Uruguay](/interests/nature/tours/uruguay/), check the country where each nature-focused day actually takes place: on multi-country tours it may be outside Uruguay.

## Allocating days for wildlife watching

From a nature perspective, the journey contains several different types of days:

| Stage | Actual focus |
|---|---|
| Galápagos | Tortoises and a marine excursion |
| Atacama | Scenery and altitude |
| Guatapé | Rocks and reservoir |
| Montevideo | Historic city |

For the island section, allow time for the flight through mainland Ecuador, the crossing to Santa Cruz and the scheduled excursion day. Shortening the island stay to add another country reduces the opportunities for wildlife watching. One confirmed island excursion cannot be replaced with another without agreement.

Ada Tours helps travelers match the entire transfer sequence to their interests. If birds, tortoises and marine wildlife are the priority, review the [Galápagos program](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) and the actual excursion route. Travelers seeking geographic variety can explore the [general four-country selection](/multi-country/chile_colombia_ecuador_uruguay/), while the [multi-country Wildlife and Safaris catalog](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) offers a broader search.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in the four countries

### Will we see animals in all four countries?

The current itinerary provides no basis for such a promise. The main wildlife experiences are in the Galápagos, while Uruguay and much of Colombia are represented by city sightseeing.

### Can North Seymour be selected in advance?

The tour description includes one of two island alternatives. The chosen route is confirmed at booking; visiting North Seymour should be agreed separately.

### Does the tour include a safari in the Colombian Amazon?

No. The Colombian stage covers Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. The [full itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) shows every day before you choose the trip.

  Chile, Peru and Colombia offer three distinct South American experiences in one journey: the Atacama Desert, Inca heritage and Colombian cities. ## Chile, Peru and Colombia: why the route includes more countries

The combination of [Chile](/chile/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) appeals to travelers who want to experience the Atacama, Inca monuments and historic cities near the Caribbean. This selection, however, identifies countries on a confirmed itinerary, **not a separate tour visiting only these three countries**.

On the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), the route passes through Bolivia after Chile, then through Peru and Ecuador before Colombia. The active selection is recalculated alongside the site's tour catalog: {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}.

A shorter trip would require a new agreement on the country sequence and number of flights. Traveling directly between Santiago, Lima and Bogotá would be a different travel product.

## Experiences actually included in the itinerary

| Country | Main places |
|---|---|
| Chile | Santiago, Atacama |
| Peru | Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lima |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá |

**Chile.** The Chilean section begins with [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), its central squares and a sightseeing excursion. Next comes a flight to Calama, a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and preparation for the high-altitude continuation. An evening telescope observation is available as an optional activity and must not be treated as included.

**Peru.** After the Bolivian highlands, travelers arrive in the area of [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The route then covers [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and sightseeing in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). This is a historical and cultural section where the visit schedule matters more than squeezing in extra short stops.

**Colombia.** From Ecuador, the program continues to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), then visits [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and Comuna 13. After a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the journey concludes in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with an excursion to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). This combines a city in a mountain valley, the Caribbean coast and a high-altitude capital.

## Where additional borders lie

Between Chile and Peru, the current tour passes through Bolivia's lagoons, Uyuni, La Paz and Tiwanaku. Travelers do not continue directly from Peru to Colombia: they first visit [Quito and the equatorial area](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), then the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), before returning to mainland Ecuador.

The “Chile + Peru + Colombia” filter therefore cannot be treated as a ready-made flight itinerary without intervening countries. Removing Bolivia changes the high-altitude section; excluding Ecuador removes the island stage and alters the flights. Travelers focused on the Andes may also find the [Chile and Peru combination](/multi-country/chile_peru/) useful.

## Altitude, weather and the actual pace

In the [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), strong sun and dry air contrast with cool evenings; altitude is particularly noticeable on Bolivia's Altiplano and around Titicaca. Later, the route passes through Pacific-coast Lima, Medellín's mountain valley and warm Cartagena. There is no single “South American weather” pattern: choose clothing and luggage based on specific days.

At altitude, a measured pace and attention to acclimatization are important. Anyone with cardiovascular or respiratory illness, who is pregnant, or who has other medical restrictions should discuss the route with their doctor in advance; insurance should be checked for geographic and activity coverage. Pack a warm layer, comfortable closed-toe shoes and light clothing for the tropical coast.

Domestic flights come with separate baggage weight allowances and check-in requirements. We help coordinate the sequence of stops and sensible connections, but the exact allowances must be confirmed with the carriers chosen for the itinerary.

## Documents and money in the three countries

For holders of **ordinary Russian international passports**, official sources checked on October 16, 2026, described short-term visa-free tourist entry to Chile and Colombia. Requirements for Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and transit countries must be checked separately for the travel dates. Passport validity, proof of onward travel, possible re-entry and connecting-flight rules all matter. Other nationalities will face different requirements.

The currencies are the Chilean peso in Chile, the sol in Peru and the Colombian peso in Colombia. Even if you bring US dollars, they cannot be guaranteed as an accepted payment method everywhere. International payment cards issued by Russian banks are not suitable for routine payments abroad; whether any other card works depends on its issuing bank. It is wise to plan cash reserves, currency exchange and payment methods for excursions and personal expenses in advance.

When entering Chile, plant and animal products must be declared if present in luggage. This is particularly important after purchases in previous countries.

## Choosing the current tour

To compare the actual itinerary, duration and published prices, consult the relevant tour listing rather than a hypothetical budget for a trip visiting just three countries:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If Machu Picchu and Colombia are your main priorities, we can help identify the essential parts of the full itinerary, the countries that could be considered separately and where extra time is needed. Any route change requires a new agreement on terms.

## Frequently asked questions about Chile, Peru and Colombia

### Can I visit just these three countries in two weeks?

Such a trip can be planned individually, but the current selection does not establish the existence of a ready-made two-week tour. The complete published itinerary lasts 32 days and includes eight countries.

### Will we travel directly from Chile to Peru?

Not on this tour. Bolivia, including Uyuni and La Paz, lies in between. A direct alternative would require a different transport plan.

### Will altitude be an issue throughout the route?

No, conditions vary by stop. Altitude is more demanding on the highland section; the preparation changes when descending to the ocean and visiting Cartagena. Your tolerance of altitude should be assessed in advance.

### Can I pay everywhere with one bank card?

There is no guarantee. For Chile, Peru and Colombia, check the issuing bank, payment network, local currencies and cash reserves beforehand.

lead: >-
  The combination of Chile, Colombia and Peru offers the Atacama's dry landscapes, mountain views around Guatapé and a high-altitude route through Puno and Cusco to Machu Picchu. The current Ada Tours itinerary covers eight countries over 32 days. ## What kind of adventure does the Chile, Colombia and Peru route offer?

**A combination of three countries does not mean three separate trekking expeditions.** On the available [32-day South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), Chile brings the Atacama, Peru Lake Titicaca, high-altitude transfers and Machu Picchu, and Colombia the mountain panoramas of Guatapé and major cities. Adventure is an additional theme of the tour, but the physical demands vary from day to day.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring these main countries. The current itinerary also visits Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Ecuador. **The longest off-road section is a two-day 4x4 jeep journey in Bolivia**, after leaving San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. Presenting it as a jeep expedition through Chile itself would be inaccurate.

Explore other travel formats in the [general country-combination catalog](/multi-country/chile_colombia_peru/), or choose trips by activity in the [multi-country adventure catalog](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Chile: why San Pedro de Atacama is the crucial starting point

After [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the route flies to Calama and continues to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The Atacama Desert and its highlands require very different preparation from an ordinary city excursion: dry air, intense sunshine, significant day-to-night temperature fluctuations and further gains in elevation.

A night near San Pedro helps travelers transition from the flight to the following road journeys. The group then heads to the Bolivian border and begins an off-road journey through Laguna Verde, high-altitude lagoons and geothermal areas toward Uyuni. This stage is part of the same longer itinerary but **geographically takes place mainly in Bolivia**. When browsing [adventure journeys including Chile](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/), distinguish the Chilean base, the border crossing itself and the onward route.

An optional astronomy excursion near San Pedro is mentioned as a possibility, not a mandatory part of the tour. A classic desert trek or a volcano ascent cannot be considered included without separate confirmation. On this itinerary, the adventure lies primarily in the roads and high-altitude conditions.

## Peru: Machu Picchu and Titicaca without confusing sightseeing with trekking

The Peruvian section begins after traveling from La Paz via Tiwanaku and the border crossing at Desaguadero. Around [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the itinerary includes a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). A tourist bus then travels via Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, La Raya Pass and Pucará to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). The many stops introduce the geography of the Andes, but this bus journey should not be portrayed as a separate athletic trek.

The following day features **a full-day group excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/)** with an English-speaking guide and lunch included. The historic sanctuary stands among steep mountain slopes and is recognized by UNESCO for its mixed natural and cultural heritage. However, the particular tour does not include a multi-day Inca Trail hike, camping nights or a mountaineering program.

After Machu Picchu come the attractions of Cusco and a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Altitude, transport and the type of excursion change rapidly. Participants should discuss how they cope with altitude, their walking pace and any personal medical contraindications. A specialized trekking trip should explicitly specify walking stages, distances, overnight stays and guidance.

## Colombia: an active day at Guatapé or city sightseeing?

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), there is an excursion to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), the reservoir and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). It lasts around 8 hours, includes a visit to a replica of old El Peñol and exploration of the town; part of the Guatapé visit is by motorcycle taxi. Driving, walking, scenic viewpoints and cultural stops alternate throughout the day.

Visiting the rock **does not mean rock climbing is included**. Roped climbing, rafting and an extended mountain trek are not advertised for this day. The itinerary continues via Cartagena and Bogotá, focusing mainly on historic neighborhoods, museums and the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá.

If sporting activity is the priority, compare [adventure tours in Colombia](/interests/adventure/tours/colombia/) according to specific activities rather than the mountains shown in photographs.

## Logistics, physical demands and expenses: what to compare

A single journey combines flights, mountain road sections and border crossings. The Chilean section gives way to high-altitude Bolivia, followed by Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Sharp changes in altitude and temperature may matter more than the distance traveled. After active days on the road, travelers need opportunities to rest, sleep and avoid compressing several long excursions into one day.

| Stage | Actual format |
|---|---|
| San Pedro de Atacama | Base before the Bolivian off-road stage |
| Puno–Cusco | Tourist bus with stops |
| Machu Picchu | Full-day group excursion |
| Medellín–Guatapé | Guided excursion and scenic stops |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

This tour includes 4-star hotels and domestic flights, but which excursions are paid for should be checked day by day. Entry rules for the various countries must be reviewed according to nationality and transit route. Chile uses Chilean pesos, Peru soles and Colombia Colombian pesos. A particular bank card's usability and access to cash cannot be guaranteed without checking before departure.

Ada Tours helps coordinate transport stages, guides and transfers and clarify which days involve physical exertion. For a customized sporting itinerary, the difficulty, duration, equipment and relevant restrictions are agreed in advance; activities from neighboring programs are not automatically carried over.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Chile, Colombia and Peru

### Does the tour include an Inca Trail trek to Machu Picchu?

No. The 32-day itinerary includes a one-day group excursion to Machu Picchu. No multi-day hike with overnight stays is specified.

### Where does the jeep expedition take place?

It begins after departing San Pedro de Atacama and crossing the border, and continues through Bolivia's high-altitude areas. Chile is the starting point, but the route is not limited to the three selected countries.

### Is Guatapé a rock-climbing tour?

No. Visiting the rock and viewing the reservoir are part of a sightseeing day; climbing with equipment and an instructor is not confirmed.

### Is the tour suitable without specialized sporting training?

Most of the listed stops are sightseeing excursions. However, altitude, long transfers and the duration of the trip require consideration of your health and usual pace. Conditions for any active pursuits should be checked before booking.

### Can I visit only Chile, Colombia and Peru?

The current ready-made product covers eight countries. A route through only three countries must be planned separately: the other stages cannot simply be removed without changing the whole logistics and duration.

## What links the cultures of Chile, Peru and Colombia on one journey?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers Chile, Peru and Colombia, alongside Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Ecuador. This is one long itinerary, not a separate three-country program with direct transfers between the selected countries.

The three cultural sections offer different experiences. In Chile, travelers explore the capital's historic center and urban life; in Peru, they encounter Inca heritage, Andean settlements and old Lima; in Colombia, they discover how colonial neighborhoods coexist with the new culture of major cities. Compare other themed destinations in the [multi-country culture and history catalog](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/), or use the [Chile, Colombia and Peru combination](/multi-country/chile_colombia_peru/) to see itineraries regardless of theme.

## Chile: Santiago before the high-altitude crossing

The Chilean cultural section centers on [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A guided tour of the capital with a Russian-speaking guide includes the La Moneda government district, [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/) and Santa Lucía Hill. It is a good way to understand the historic heart of the city and get your bearings for independent walks.

The following day takes the group via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The purpose is different here: adjusting to altitude before the overland section through Bolivia. A night-time astronomy excursion is an optional service and should not be counted among the cultural experiences unconditionally included.

If the capital itself is your main interest, compare [cultural and historical tours including Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/). The longer journey makes sense if you want to explore other eras and countries after Santiago.

## Peru: Inca heritage, Lake Titicaca and Lima

The itinerary enters Peru through the [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) area. An excursion to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) introduces life on the floating reed islands. From there, a bus travels to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with stops at Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani and other Andean locations. These stops are meaningful in their own right, connecting archaeology, local traditions and contemporary towns.

A separate day is devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the Inca archaeological complex in the mountains. The trip includes rail travel, a group excursion with an English-speaking guide and a return to Cusco. Machu Picchu is known for its stone architecture integrated into the mountain landscape and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The day after Machu Picchu is spent around Cusco: Qorikancha, Q'enqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuamán. A flight to Lima follows, where the program combines Miraflores, the main square and Santo Domingo Monastery. Peru offers the most archaeology of these three countries, so cutting its section to add another brief city stop is not always worthwhile.

## Colombia: cities, art and historic architecture

The Colombian route begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). After a trip to the Guatapé area, the itinerary includes [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), where street art is connected with the city's recent history. Travelers then fly to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and explore its historic neighborhoods.

In Bogotá, the itinerary covers city sightseeing and Monserrate, followed the next day by [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. This offers a striking contrast with Peru: rather than monuments of the Inca state, the focus shifts to colonial architecture, urban history and an unusual place of worship built in former salt mines.

Travelers seeking more time in Cartagena, Bogotá or Medellín should first explore [cultural tours in Colombia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) and compare the stops included.

## How the countries connect and why the order matters

On the current tour, **Bolivia comes after Chile and before Peru**, while **Ecuador, including the Galápagos Islands, lies between Peru and Colombia**. These are essential considerations for time and budget. The three selected countries — Chile, Peru and Colombia — are part of an eight-country itinerary; selecting them does not remove the remaining stages, flights and accommodation.

When choosing, compare four factors: days devoted to the excursions themselves, time spent on flights and road transfers, tolerance of Andean altitude and the guide language listed for each day. For example, this tour includes Russian-speaking guides in Santiago, Cusco and Lima, while the Machu Picchu excursion is conducted in English. Such details significantly affect the experience of historic sites.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the country sequence, transfers and time between excursions, and identify the documents required for the traveler's nationality. A customized program could emphasize Peruvian archaeology or Colombian cities. The included services and dates would be agreed separately.

## Frequently asked questions about the cultural route

### Can I visit only Chile, Peru and Colombia on this itinerary?

The ready-made [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers eight countries. A program visiting exactly three would need to be designed separately: Bolivia and Ecuador lie between them on the original route, so other days cannot be removed without changing the logistics.

### Where are the most ancient monuments?

On the confirmed program, Peru has the most extensive archaeological section: Cusco, Machu Picchu and stops along the Andean road. The Chilean and Colombian days focus mainly on urban history and cultural life.

### Do I need to prepare for altitude?

Yes, if San Pedro de Atacama, the Bolivian highlands and the crossings through the Andes remain on the route. Time to acclimatize in the Atacama is built into the itinerary; personal altitude tolerance and health should be considered before final confirmation.

### Are all cultural excursions included in the stated price?

The tour includes the excursions and admission tickets specified in the program, but some optional activities cost extra. Check the [full list of tour services](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/): Maipo Valley wineries and the astronomy excursion in the Atacama are optional.

lead: >-
  On the Ada Tours route, nature in Chile, Peru and Colombia is revealed through sharp changes in altitude: the arid north of Chile, high-altitude Lake Titicaca and the green valleys around Machu Picchu, followed by the hills near Colombia's Guatapé. ## From the Atacama to Guatapé: the natural progression across three countries

Our Chile, Colombia and Peru nature selection features a [long journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). **These countries represent a subset of its geography, not a ready-made independent trip directly from Chile to Peru and Colombia.** After Chile, travelers pass through Bolivia, then Peru, and visit Ecuador before reaching Colombia.

Each country's natural highlights are different: Chile offers a stark dry desert, Peru a high Andean lake and mountain ecosystems, and Colombia green terrain around a reservoir. When choosing, consider not only the names of natural attractions but also altitude, how they are reached, travel distances and the actual excursion format.

| Stage | Confirmed stops |
|---|---|
| Chile | San Pedro de Atacama |
| Peru | Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu |
| Colombia | El Peñón, Guatapé |

The parent [Chile, Colombia and Peru catalog](/multi-country/chile_colombia_peru/) has no thematic restriction. This page explains which experiences are nature-focused and which remain historical or urban parts of the same tour.

## Chile: a nature stop before serious altitude

After Santiago, the itinerary includes a flight via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The area is known for dry air, desert landscapes and significant temperature changes between day and night. **This stop prepares travelers for the following jeep crossing into Bolivia**, where the route passes high-altitude lagoons, geothermal fields and salt flats.

Laguna Verde, Laguna Colorada and the Uyuni Salt Flat that follow are already in Bolivia. They cannot be listed as Chilean excursions simply because the trip departs from San Pedro. An evening astronomy activity is offered separately in Chile; an extended expedition visiting every Atacama attraction is not guaranteed.

The high-altitude sections of the following days exceed 4,000 meters, as the program explicitly states. It is therefore more important to allow for rest, warm clothing and drinking water, and to discuss any personal medical limitations, than to pack the short Chilean section with as many stops as possible.

## Peru: Lake Titicaca and changing mountain ecosystems

After Bolivia, the route crosses the border at Desaguadero and reaches [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A visit to the floating Uros Islands is planned for the afternoon. The lake lies at approximately 3,825 meters above sea level, so even an easy excursion takes place in high-altitude conditions. Sun, wind and cool air call for suitable clothing and a gentle pace.

The following day, a tourist bus travels via Andahuaylillas, Raqchi and La Raya Pass to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). The road offers views of the Andes, but **does not promise separate treks across every valley along the way**: some stops are primarily historical or cultural.

An excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) follows. For nature lovers, the attraction lies not only in the Inca ruins but also in the surrounding mountains, cloud forests and transition from the high Andes to more humid slopes. The current program provides a one-day group excursion, returning to Cusco by train. An independent Inca Trail trek or an ascent of any chosen mountain summit is not automatically included.

The contrast is pronounced: the open, cold highlands around Titicaca and the greener slopes near Machu Picchu belong to the same country but call for different clothing and pacing.

## Colombia: El Peñón Rock and a reservoir rather than high-altitude desert

The Colombian nature stop comes after Ecuador. From Medellín, travelers go to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The view takes in green hills, small islands and a reservoir. Unlike the mountain lagoons of the Chilean–Bolivian highlands, the landscape here contains a large man-made body of water.

The day's main nature experience is the panorama and the surrounding countryside near Medellín. **Climbing the rock involves stairs and physical exertion**: the availability and duration of the ascent must be checked against the actual excursion plan and personal fitness. The route then continues to Cartagena and Bogotá, with mainly urban, historical and cultural activities.

Travelers who primarily want long hikes in Colombia's mountains may find a single scenic excursion to Guatapé insufficient. The confirmed 32-day itinerary does not include a separate multi-day mountain hike in Colombia.

## Altitude and numerous transfers: what to consider

The main risk in this combination is treating every nature-focused day as though it involved the same physical exertion. In fact, elevations above 4,000 meters occur on the route from Chile through Bolivia; Peru brings Titicaca and mountainous Cusco; Colombia's nature day involves traveling to a rock and walking.

For northern Chile and the highlands, bring sun protection, covering clothing, a warm layer and footwear suitable for uneven terrain. Rain and wet trails are possible around Machu Picchu; light rain protection is also useful in Colombia. When choosing travel dates, compare conditions in every region and allow extra time for flights and road transfers instead of relying on a single country's season.

The journey crosses several borders beyond the three named countries. Entry, transit, passport validity, insurance requirements and permitted medications or altitude-related medical advice must be checked separately for each nationality. Ada Tours helps organize the transfer sequence, but cannot guarantee altitude tolerance or compliance with border rules without the traveler's personal documentation.

## Who this combination suits

Chile and Peru will appeal to travelers who want to experience **high-altitude South America in several forms**: the dry Atacama, salt flats en route and Lake Titicaca, followed by the mountain forests of Machu Picchu. Colombia adds the very different green panorama of Guatapé and completes the nature experiences with a contrast to the Andes.

To focus on the mountain route and reduce transfers, compare [nature trips in Chile](/interests/nature/tours/chile/) and [nature programs in Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/). If Colombia's green landscapes are particularly important, explore [nature tours in Colombia](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/). A shorter version's duration and activities would be set in a customized itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about nature on the Chile–Peru–Colombia journey

### Can Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu be visited on one tour?

Yes. On the confirmed itinerary, Puno and the Uros Islands follow the crossing from Bolivia, with Cusco and a separate day trip to Machu Picchu afterward.

### Will I have to hike into the mountains every day?

No. The route combines domestic flights, road transfers, excursions and short walks. The Inca Trail hike and a multi-day Colombian trek are not mandatory parts of this program.

### Is Uyuni part of Chile or Peru?

Neither. Uyuni and the high-altitude lagoons reached after leaving San Pedro are in Bolivia. That country is part of the complete eight-country route but not the title of this selection.

### Is there a separate three-country itinerary without the other five nations?

The current thematic selection features one long tour through eight countries. A shortened Chile–Peru–Colombia journey must be designed and agreed separately.
